proposals: RBI should publish a periodic list of specific approvals granted beyond the automatic route under the Overseas Direct Investment rules, with the company, amount and type of commitment, so dispensations like the one this deal needed can be confirmed from the regulator rather than from press reports.

RBI should publish a review of whether the $1 billion ODI guarantee limit should be aligned with the External Commercial Borrowings ceiling widened in February 2026, so the gap between the two frameworks that this deal exposed is addressed on the record.

SEBI should require listed companies announcing outbound acquisitions above a set size to disclose, in the exchange filing, the financing structure and every regulatory approval the financing still depends on, so shareholders can see dependencies such as an RBI exception at announcement.

Public-sector banks such as SBI should disclose, in their annual reports, total commitments to financing overseas acquisitions by Indian companies, so the growing PSU-bank role in deals of this size is visible to depositors and shareholders.
